_meta.note: Additional settings-window strings (module fragment): merged with en.json, keys here win.

general.defaultMode: Default conversation mode (applies on the next start; /mode switches it immediately)
general.pathBackend: Backend folder (config / models / session / automation log)
general.themeHelp: Pick the colour scheme. “Follow system” tracks the Windows app mode.
general.themeNote: Theme and emoji settings apply immediately, no restart needed.
general.emojiHelp: Auto: show colour icons when the emoji font is present, otherwise fall back to plain tags such as [OK].
general.emojiOn: Emoji font found — icons render normally
general.emojiForcedOff: Using plain text tags as you requested
general.emojiFontMissing: The emoji font is missing on this system; the UI falls back to plain tags ([OK] / [!])
general.pathUserData: User data folder (UI state / snippets / batch results)
general.pathPortableNote: Note: this build uses the portable layout — the program itself lives in app\, while ui_state.json, snippets and the batch results folder sit in the outer directory for easy backup and migration.
general.confirmOff: Command confirmation is OFF (commands with side effects run immediately)

automation.helpPlaceholderBody: Put the cursor into any input below (or click the ? next to a field) and this panel explains that field in plain words, with an example. The full guide is at docs\<locale>\AUTOMATION_GUIDE.md in the release package.
automation.pickDetailTip: Opens the first task automatically, then you click the attachment name on the detail page
automation.pickLoginTip: After signing in, click an element on the page that only appears once you are signed in (for example the user name in the corner)
automation.loginHint: Automation keeps its sign-in state (cookies and so on) in a separate browser data directory that is never shared with your everyday browser. On the first run the program opens the browser so you can sign in manually; after that the state is reused, so you do not sign in again every time.
automation.clearLoginTip: Deletes the browser data directory reserved for automation; the next run asks you to sign in manually again
automation.clearLoginConfirm:
Clear the automation sign-in state?

Afterwards the next run asks you to sign in manually once in the browser window that opens.
(This does not affect your everyday browser and does not delete any result files.)
automation.clearLoginFailed: ❌ Failed to clear the sign-in state: {0}
automation.loginMultiSite: Several target sites can share one data directory (the browser stores cookies per domain), so there is no need to configure each site separately.
automation.loginStateEmpty: Sign-in state: not saved yet ({0} does not exist). The first automation run guides you through signing in manually in the browser.
automation.loginStateLegacy: The old browser_state.json backup is still present.
automation.loginStateFailed: Sign-in state: could not be read ({0})
automation.pickDiscarded: ↩️ This selection was discarded (the configuration was not changed); please click the target element again.

label.taskDetailFileSelector: Attachment position on the detail page
label.instruction: Task instruction (concatenated with the file content for the local model)
label.loginStateDir: Data directory (empty = browser_profile inside the program directory)
label.loginCheckSelector: Element that appears only after signing in (optional, used to detect the sign-in state)
label.loginKeywords: Sign-in page URL keywords (comma separated, fallback detection)
label.enabled: Enable automation (the safety protocol is still required before each run)

automation.enabledNeedsSafety: Enable automation (tick the safety protocol above first)

automation.resultsDirOpenFailed: ❌ Failed to open the result folder: {0}
automation.resultsLocationPrompt: Choose where to save batch results
automation.needUrlAndSelector: ❌ Fill in the task list URL and the element position first
automation.safetyRequiredText: Read and accept the safety protocol before running automation.
automation.stopRequested: ⏹ Stop requested; waiting for the current step to finish…
